label: Potentially dangerous
explanation: The model predicts the combined risk class: phishing, malware or defacement. It cannot identify the subtype.

signals.title: Hidden destination
signals.detail: Text before @ is not the real destination host. It is the URL's sign-in information; a familiar name here does not mean you are visiting that site.

signals.title: IP address as host
signals.detail: This link uses a numeric IP address instead of a named website. That makes the organisation behind it harder to recognise; legitimate services can also use IP addresses.

signals.title: Brand in a subdomain
signals.detail: A familiar brand appears in the prefix of the hostname. That prefix does not establish ownership by the brand; check the base domain and the complete host.

signals.title: Look-alike characters
signals.detail: Some characters resemble Latin letters but have different Unicode values. They can be legitimate language characters, yet make an unfamiliar address look familiar. This check covers only a limited character list.

signals.title: Encoded URL characters
signals.detail: Percent codes represent characters, while xn-- marks an internationalised domain. Both are normal URL formats, but can make the address harder to read. Decoding shown here is for reading only; it does not change the destination or model input.

signals.title: Account-related terms
signals.detail: Words about signing in, accounts or verification appear in the address. Real login pages use these words too; their presence does not prove that the site is malicious.

signals.title: Many subdomains
signals.detail: Several labels precede the base domain. They can make a long hostname harder to recognise, though legitimate sites also use subdomains.

signals.title: Long URL
signals.detail: This address is longer than the 120-character display rule. Long links can hide important parts, but search, sharing and tracking links are often long too.

signals.title: HTTP without TLS
signals.detail: The address starts with HTTP rather than HTTPS, so it does not request an encrypted HTTPS connection. We have not connected to the site or checked its certificate.

signals.title: Unusual connection port
signals.detail: This URL names a port other than the usual HTTP port 80 or HTTPS port 443. Development tools and legitimate services can also use custom ports.

signals.title: Brand words outside the host
signals.detail: A familiar brand appears in the path or parameters. Those words do not determine which website receives the request; they can also occur in legitimate articles, search results and links.

disclaimer: DTDLINK analyses URL text only. It does not visit the website. A benign prediction does not guarantee safety.
